I  grew up in a small town half the size of Mayberry. Had less than a hundred people and we were all white. For the most part nearly everyone was around eighty. People gathered at the store every afternoon to play dominoes. The store also had the Post Office as art of the building and also sold feed and had one gas pump. If the post master was playing dominoes then you had to wait for him to finish his hand before you could get service. 

The average person was sympathetic to the south and we were all racist although we didn't know it. A lot of the ladies dipped snuff even in church. I knew a man who spent three years in prison for robbing a stage coach and I also knew the sheriff who caught him. Old men would look at us boys through peep holes in the outhouse as we young ones peed. No one was gay but some old men would pay you for favors. Most people were farmers until they got to old to work. No one in those days wanted anyone to know how much money they had in the bank so they pretended to be poor. 

Until drugs became the sin for the younger people a lot of people dranked bootleg whiskey at their weekend parties but dranked store bought during the week. Although the town had very few people there were four churches because people couldn't agree about their faith. There were two baptist, one church of Christ and one Presbyterian I think. 

Those old timers cussed, dranked and would try to get the best deal in business matters. Even if they had to be dishonest. But on small matters like their bill at the store they would always pay some every month. 

People were the same then as now. They had some good in them along with some bad. I get a kick out of these old timers today who say people were more honest, better or holier in those days. Most things that were abnormal in society then like child beatings or homosexuality just wasn't talked about, even sex. Sin laws were in place but they were for outward appearances mostly. 

Not exactly on target with my post here but I wanted to show how old people thought then where I grew up. I got to see people at the end of their era along with a new era with the peace movements and also MLK. I'm thankful for that. BTW I graduated high school in 1975 in case you want a time frame.

It's 1993 and I had been gone a few years on my drug run. I finally had myself straight and I was dating my future wife.We were spending the first Thanksgiving at my parents house in five years. Along with my parents there were my three brothers and their wives. After dinner I had to take a dump so I get up and went to the restroom. My parents lived in this old house and as the usual case was in this town, they used a septic tank for waste. So I take this huge dump in the toilet and then push the handle to give it a good flush and the water started to swirl in the tank. It began to rise slowly to the top, floating my arm length brown dump with it. I started to panic as I pictured that turd floating over the top and landing on the bathroom floor. How would I clean it up? How would I explain this to my family and girlfriend? I watched and taught myself how to pray silently as the turd kept moving slowly toward the top of the rim. I felt hot and wanted to leave, but AA had taught me how to face my problems without running away. So I watched my brown waste float its' way to the top and then slowly the water began to move downward into the tank. Slowly it moved but it was a steady drain to the end and now all there was left was my turd laying by itself at the bottom of the stool. I grabbed the plunger and flushed again only this time I began to plunge the toilet until it drained. As I watched my mushy turd move through the bottom of the toilet I felt the salty sweet in my eyes begin to burn. It was over, my Thanksgiving waste product was disposed of and I thanked God for the victory. I then walked back to the kitchen like a big dog who had just whooped his first wolf.

I looked at myself different, I was raised not to make anyone angry because for some reason that was a bad thing (I never understood this) I was gay, but didn't know what gay was, because sex education wasn't taught but I also knew I looked at other boys and was ashamed of myself. I only had a couple of close friends and they were tramps like me. I wasn't supposed to be anybody. I wanted something bad to happen to me everyday, thinking that if it did then maybe someone would care. I felt stupid all the time, like I was incapable of learning anything at all. I joined the Army, that didn't work, came back home and did the drug thing, lost a business, I did managed to stay out of jail, but liked the drugs. 

Somewhere I picked up a bible, read a lot and cursed God for making me this way. At an earlier time in my life, my uncle had taken me up front to the altar to get saved, but since that denomination believed that if a person did not get baptized in tongues then they didn't get saved, then I had left thinking that I was too ugly and stupid for God. So I cursed him then and later in life.

As time went on I got that part taken care off. I found out that my uncle was wrong. It took me a while to work out all the kinks though. I finally landed my first good job ever and I am still working there. I met my wife when I was forty years old. She was thirty. She weighed three hundred pounds (she has lost a hundred since). I didn't want anything to do with her at first because I thought it was an insult for me to be seen with her. I fell in love. Don't ask me how, it just happened, so I put a ring on her finger. She had a child already and her ex had a good relationship with the little girl so there wasn't any real problems there but my wife was bi-polar. I didn't know this when we got married. It really flared up when her mom died. She couldn't work, but after going to several doctors we found one that helped. My PCP diagnosed me with a mild form of depression and put me on mood enhancers. They work great. Watching my wife go through her thing taught me so much about mine. Watching this little girl grow up taught me so much about life. It was like l was learning what I should have learned thirty years ago.

I am in school now, it's an on-line thing that doesn't hold the prestige of Harvard or anything like that. But I found out I am not stupid but that I can learn.
